breakthroughs.title: Formal Lean Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis & Dirichlet GRH
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Resolves mathematics' most iconic Millennium Prize Problem—and Dirichlet GRH—with a machine-checked Lean 4 proof verified by the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative.
breakthroughs.summary: On November 20, 2026, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released a formal Lean 4 proof of both the classical Riemann Hypothesis and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, developed over six weeks alongside an unreleased research model of Claude. Within 24 hours, the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative confirmed the formalization compiles cleanly against standard axioms. Initially spanning ~17 million lines of Lean code, the proof was refactored to ~300,000 lines by Luke Sernau five days later.
technicalHighlights: Proves all non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function and Dirichlet L-functions lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2.
Draws on deep machinery spanning modern number theory, the Langlands program, and arithmetic geometry.
Verified by Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative on Nov 21, 2026; compressed 56× from 17M to 300k lines by Nov 25, 2026.
breakthroughs.caveats: No complete human-readable mathematical exposition exists yet. While the Lean kernel guarantees logical soundness relative to the stated definitions, mathematicians are actively auditing whether the formal definitions match classical conventions and extracting human intuition from the proof.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolves the foremost open problem in pure mathematics since Bernhard Riemann's 1859 paper, plus Dirichlet GRH.
scoreRationale.ripple: Converts hundreds of conditional theorems across prime distribution, analytic number theory, and primality algorithms into unconditional truths.
scoreRationale.verification: Machine-verified in Lean 4 by independent Lean FRO and Mathlib teams, docked slightly pending a full human-readable monograph.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed what many mathematicians considered a multi-decade or century-scale open problem into a six-week human–AI collaboration.

breakthroughs.title: AlphaProof Code: Machine-Code Formal Verification of Signal Protocol
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: First protocol-level mathematical security proofs for the unmodified compiled machine code of a globally deployed cryptographic protocol—completed in four weeks.
breakthroughs.summary: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent AI system that produced machine-checked Lean proofs establishing core security guarantees—including post-compromise security and post-quantum key exchange properties—directly on the compiled AArch64 Linux binary of Signal's unmodified libsignal (v0.105.4) and SPQR (v1.6.0) Rust crates. A five-person team completed the verification in four weeks.
technicalHighlights: Operates directly on compiled AArch64 machine code rather than idealized abstract protocol models, eliminating compiler and implementation-gap vulnerabilities.
Proves post-compromise security and post-quantum key exchange guarantees in Lean.
Demonstrates an order-of-magnitude reduction in the human-effort cost of formal verification for production software.
breakthroughs.caveats: Proof guarantees hold relative to the formal security specification and trusted computing base (§5.3 of the technical paper); hardware side-channels and out-of-spec runtime assumptions remain outside the verified boundary.

scoreRationale.foundational: Breaks the decades-old scalability barrier separating formal methods from real-world compiled cryptographic software.
scoreRationale.ripple: Establishes a practical blueprint for mathematically verifying critical infrastructure: OS kernels, TLS stacks, browsers, and avionics.
scoreRationale.verification: Machine-checked Lean proofs with public specifications and verification artifacts released for independent inspection.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed what historically required tens of person-years of formal-methods labor into four weeks with five researchers.

breakthroughs.title: Proof of the Geometric Langlands Conjecture
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Completes a monumental 'grand unified theory' bridge in mathematics connecting categories of sheaves on algebraic curves with Galois-side spectral data.
breakthroughs.summary: Dennis Gaitsgory, Sam Raskin, and seven collaborators published a five-paper, ~1,000-page proof of the global, unramified categorical Geometric Langlands Conjecture in characteristic zero. Culminating three decades of research initiated by Beilinson and Drinfeld, the proof establishes an exact equivalence between automorphic D-modules on Bun_G and ind-coherent sheaves with nilpotent singular support on the stack of local systems for the Langlands dual group.
technicalHighlights: Spans five coordinated arXiv papers (May–September 2024) constructing the Langlands functor, Kac–Moody localization, ambidexterity, and multiplicity one.
Realizes a central pillar of the broader Langlands Program linking geometry, representation theory, and S-duality in quantum field theory.
Pure human mathematical synthesis built atop derived algebraic geometry.
breakthroughs.caveats: Proves the unramified geometric conjecture in characteristic zero; the arithmetic Langlands program over number fields and ramified/positive-characteristic extensions remain active frontiers.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolves one of the defining structural conjectures of modern pure mathematics and derived algebraic geometry.
scoreRationale.ripple: Deeply informs arithmetic Langlands research, 4D gauge theory (Kapustin–Witten), and representation theory.
scoreRationale.verification: Extensively revised, peer-vetted across workshops worldwide, and widely accepted by the algebraic geometry community.
scoreRationale.velocity: Represents the culmination of a 30-year collaborative human research program rather than a sudden methodology shock.

breakthroughs.title: Simulating Time t Computations in O(√(t log t)) Space
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Shatters a 50-year barrier in theoretical computer science by proving any time-t multitape computation can be simulated using roughly square-root memory.
breakthroughs.summary: MIT complexity theorist Ryan Williams proved that every deterministic multitape Turing machine running in time t can be simulated in only O(√(t log t)) space—the first asymptotic improvement since Hopcroft, Paul, and Valiant's 1975 O(t / log t) bound. By reducing time-bounded computation to implicitly defined Tree Evaluation instances solved via the Cook–Mertz catalytic-space procedure, the theorem immediately yields stronger circuit lower bounds and restructures our map of time–space tradeoffs.
technicalHighlights: Improves the 1975 Hopcroft–Paul–Valiant bound TIME[t] ⊆ SPACE[t / log t] dramatically to TIME[t] ⊆ SPACE[√(t log t)].
Shows that memory is exponentially more reusable relative to time than previously proved.
Presented at STOC 2025 and immediately sparked follow-up improvements for circuit value and randomized/quantum space bounds.
breakthroughs.caveats: The simulation incurs a super-polynomial time overhead, so it is a structural complexity breakthrough rather than a drop-in RAM compression algorithm for practical software.

scoreRationale.foundational: Overturns a half-century standstill on the fundamental relationship between time and memory in computation.
scoreRationale.ripple: Unlocks new lower bounds against P-uniform circuits and catalyzed a wave of 2025–2026 catalytic-space results.
scoreRationale.verification: Short, clean, peer-reviewed STOC 2025 proof verified immediately by the complexity theory community.
scoreRationale.velocity: An unexpected leap from t/log t directly to √(t log t) just months after Cook–Mertz's STOC 2024 breakthrough.

breakthroughs.title: AlphaFold 3: Unified Atomic Modeling of All Biomolecular Complexes
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Extends atomic-precision structure prediction beyond isolated proteins to joint complexes of proteins, DNA, RNA, small-molecule drugs, and ions.

Substantially outperforms specialized docking tools and AlphaFold-Multimer on antibody–antigen and protein–ligand complexes.
Cited >17,000 times within two years and serves as the structural validation backbone for generative biology platforms like Evo 2.

breakthroughs.title: Proof of the 3-Dimensional Kakeya Conjecture
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Solves a century-old pillar of geometric measure theory in 3D, proving any set containing a unit line segment in every direction has full Hausdorff dimension 3.
breakthroughs.summary: Hong Wang (NYU/IAS) and Joshua Zahl (UBC) posted a 127-page proof resolving the 3-dimensional Kakeya conjecture—a problem rooted in Sōichi Kakeya's 1917 needle-rotation question and central to Fourier restriction theory and wave equations. Introducing a delicate multi-scale 'graininess' and sticky-Kakeya induction, the proof earned wide acclaim and recognition including the 2026 Fields Medal.
technicalHighlights: Proves every Besicovitch/Kakeya set in ℝ³ has Minkowski and Hausdorff dimension equal to 3.
Builds on Wang and Zahl's earlier 'sticky Kakeya' breakthrough via multi-scale tube-intersection estimates.
Catalyzed follow-up efforts—including AI-assisted attempts—to generalize the method to four and higher dimensions.
breakthroughs.caveats: Establishes the n = 3 case; higher dimensions (n ≥ 4) and the stronger Kakeya maximal function conjecture remain separate hurdles under active investigation.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolves one of the crown jewels of harmonic analysis and geometric measure theory open for over a century.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly advances Fourier restriction, dispersive PDEs, and incidence geometry.
scoreRationale.verification: Thoroughly vetted by harmonic analysis leaders including Terence Tao, with multiple expository surveys published in 2025–2026.
scoreRationale.velocity: Breakthrough synthesis overcoming a decades-long logjam beyond the 2D (1971) case.

breakthroughs.title: AlphaEvolve: Evolutionary Coding Agent & 48-Multiplication 4×4 Matrix Algorithm
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: First AI coding agent to simultaneously break a 56-year mathematical record (Strassen's 1969 4×4 matrix bound) and optimize production data centers and chip circuits.
breakthroughs.summary: Google DeepMind introduced AlphaEvolve, an evolutionary coding agent pairing Gemini LLMs with automated evaluators to iteratively mutate and verify entire codebases. Across 50+ open math problems it matched or improved state-of-the-art constructions—most famously finding a 48-scalar-multiplication algorithm for 4×4 complex matrices (beating Strassen's 49 from 1969)—while also recovering 0.7% of Google's worldwide compute via scheduling heuristics and speeding up FlashAttention and TPU matrix circuits.
technicalHighlights: Discovered a provably exact rank-48 algorithm for multiplying 4×4 complex-valued matrices, improving on Strassen's 1969 record over ℂ.
Improved best-known mathematical bounds on ~20% of 50+ open problems (including kissing numbers in 11D).
Deployed directly into production at Google for Borg scheduling, TPU Verilog optimization, and Gemini training kernels.
breakthroughs.caveats: Requires a fast, automated objective evaluator; excels on optimization, constructive math, and verifiable code rather than open-ended physical theory without formal metrics.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated general-purpose autonomous algorithm discovery spanning both pure mathematics and real-world systems engineering.
scoreRationale.ripple: Established the LLM + verifier evolutionary search paradigm now powering quantum circuit design, hardware synthesis, and scientific discovery.
scoreRationale.verification: The 48-multiplication factorization and evolved kernels are algebraically and programmatically verified, with independent GitHub verifications.

breakthroughs.title: Below-Threshold Surface Code Quantum Error Correction (Willow)
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Experimentally proved that adding more physical qubits exponentially suppresses quantum errors—crossing the 30-year fault-tolerance threshold.
breakthroughs.summary: Published in Nature, Google Quantum AI demonstrated below-threshold surface code quantum error correction on its 105-qubit superconducting Willow processor. Scaling from distance-3 to distance-5 and distance-7 codes halved logical error rates at each step (Λ ≈ 2.14) and produced a logical qubit whose lifetime exceeded the best constituent physical qubit by more than 2×, alongside real-time decoding.
technicalHighlights: First convincing exponential error suppression as surface-code lattice size scales (d = 3 → 5 → 7).
Logical memory lifetime surpassed break-even against the best individual physical qubit on the chip.
Integrated real-time neural/algorithmic error decoding fast enough to keep pace with microsecond cycle times.
breakthroughs.caveats: Demonstrates fault-tolerant quantum memory rather than universal fault-tolerant logical gates at scale; hardware scaling to tens of thousands of physical qubits remains an engineering challenge.

scoreRationale.foundational: Validates the central experimental prerequisite of fault-tolerant quantum computation proposed in the 1990s.
scoreRationale.ripple: Triggered accelerated hardware roadmaps and enterprise post-quantum cryptography migration timelines worldwide.
scoreRationale.verification: Published in Nature (Vol. 638, pp. 920–926) with complete experimental telemetry and open datasets.
scoreRationale.velocity: Decisively cleared a hardware barrier that stalled superconducting architectures for over two decades.

breakthroughs.title: Bridge RNAs: Programmable Bispecific RNA-Guided DNA Recombinases
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Discovers a natural 'word processor for DNA' beyond CRISPR—using a single programmable RNA bridge to cleanly insert, excise, or invert large DNA segments without double-strand breaks.
breakthroughs.summary: Patrick Hsu's laboratory at the Arc Institute, collaborating with UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo, published twin Nature papers discovering that bacterial IS110 transposons encode a recombinase guided by a structured non-coding 'bridge RNA'. Unlike CRISPR—which cuts DNA and relies on error-prone cellular repair—bridge RNAs contain two independently programmable loops that specify both the target genomic site and the donor DNA sequence, enabling scarless single-step DNA insertion, excision, and inversion.
technicalHighlights: First natural DNA recombinase directed by a bispecific RNA guide specifying both target and donor DNA.
Enables large-scale genomic rearrangements (insertions, inversions, excisions) without exposing double-strand DNA breaks.
Followed by 2026 breakthroughs overcoming natural insertion bias for high-efficiency programmable excision.
breakthroughs.caveats: Initial 2024 demonstration was in bacterial systems (IS621 in E. coli); achieving high-efficiency, safe delivery and activity in primary human cells remains an active translational frontier.

scoreRationale.foundational: Uncovered an entirely new fundamental mechanism of RNA-guided nucleic acid manipulation in nature.
scoreRationale.ripple: Opens the door to whole-gene insertion, chromosome-scale synthetic biology, and safer genetic therapies beyond CRISPR.
scoreRationale.verification: Twin back-to-back Nature papers with cryo-EM structural elucidation and independent replication.
scoreRationale.velocity: Rapidly progressed from discovery (2024) to engineered bias-overcoming variants by 2026.

breakthroughs.title: Evo 2: 40B Genomic Foundation Model & Viable AI-Designed Genomes
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Trained on 9.3 trillion nucleotides across all domains of life with a 1M base-pair context, enabling zero-shot pathogenic variant prediction and wet-lab-viable AI-designed viral genomes.
breakthroughs.summary: Arc Institute, Stanford, and NVIDIA released Evo 2, a 40-billion-parameter open-source genomic foundation model trained on 9.3 trillion base pairs from over 100,000 species across prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Handling 1-million-nucleotide contexts via the StripedHyena 2 architecture, Evo 2 predicts human BRCA1 pathogenicity without task-specific training, exposes interpretable biological features (α-helices, β-sheets, exon boundaries), and by 2026 guided the chemical synthesis of viable AI-designed bacteriophage genomes capable of lysing E. coli.
technicalHighlights: 1-million-base-pair context window spans entire microbial genomes and long-range eukaryotic regulatory loci.
Mechanistic interpretability (with Goodfire) revealed learned internal representations of 3D protein secondary structure straight from raw DNA.
Downstream 2026 wet-lab validation synthesized 285 Evo-designed ΦX174 phage genomes, with 16 actively inhibiting E. coli.
breakthroughs.caveats: Viability drops steeply as generated sequences diverge from natural evolutionary neighborhoods; eukaryotic whole-genome design raises biosecurity governance challenges (prompting exclusion of human-pathogenic viruses from training).

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrates that foundation-model scaling laws and interpretability transfer directly to raw genomic sequences across all domains of life.
scoreRationale.ripple: Powers clinical variant interpretation, programmable epigenomics, and de novo synthetic genome engineering.
scoreRationale.verification: Open weights/code, bioRxiv/peer-reviewed benchmarks, and wet-lab synthesis of functional phage genomes.
scoreRationale.velocity: Moved generative biology from single protein chains to whole functional viral genomes in under two years.

breakthroughs.title: Same-Day AI Proofs of Valiant's Conjecture (VP ≠ VNP)

Backed by public Lean formalizations currently undergoing community axiom and definition audits.

breakthroughs.title: Tree Evaluation in O(log n · log log n) Space via Catalytic Computing
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Defied conventional wisdom by evaluating computation trees in nearly logarithmic space using 'borrowed' catalytic memory—directly unlocking Ryan Williams's √(t log t) theorem.
breakthroughs.summary: James Cook and Ian Mertz proved at STOC 2024 that the Tree Evaluation Problem—long proposed as a candidate to separate P from L (logarithmic space)—can actually be solved in O(log n · log log n) space. Their ingenious 'catalytic' technique temporarily overwrites full memory registers with reversible algebra and restores them afterward, shattering barriers in space complexity and directly serving as the core engine of Ryan Williams's 2025 time–space breakthrough.
technicalHighlights: Solves TreeEval in O(log n · log log n) space, overturning its long-standing role as a P ≠ L separation candidate.
Transforms catalytic computing from a curiosity into one of the most powerful tools in complexity theory.
Directly enabled Williams's 2025 TIME[t] ⊆ SPACE[√(t log t)] simulation and 2026 poly-time almost-log-space refinements.
breakthroughs.caveats: The original STOC 2024 algorithm does not simultaneously run in polynomial time, though 2026 follow-up work achieved poly-time O(log^(1+ε) n) space.

scoreRationale.foundational: Refuted the leading 14-year approach to separating L from P via an astonishingly clean algebraic reuse of memory.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly catalyzed Ryan Williams's 50-year time–space breakthrough and a resurgence in catalytic complexity.
scoreRationale.verification: Best-paper-caliber STOC 2024 result, simplified and verified across multiple expositions including Oded Goldreich's notes.
scoreRationale.velocity: An unexpected conceptual breakthrough that reshaped space complexity within months.

breakthroughs.title: Formal Lean Proof of the Existence of Non-Sofic Groups
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Resolves Mikhail Gromov's famous 1999 open question in group theory by constructing a non-sofic group—one that cannot be approximated by finite symmetric groups—with a Lean formalization.
breakthroughs.summary: In August 2026, OpenAI's internal Astra model produced a Lean-formalized proof settling the 27-year-old open question of whether every countable group is sofic. Introduced by Mikhail Gromov in 1999 and named by Benjamin Weiss, soficity generalizes amenable and residually finite groups and underpinned major results like Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture. Demonstrating that non-sofic groups exist closed one of geometric group theory's most stubborn foundational questions.
technicalHighlights: Settles a landmark open problem posed by Mikhail Gromov in 1999 across geometric group theory and ergodic theory.
Accompanied by a machine-checked Lean formalization.
Part of the mid-2026 inflection when frontier reasoning models began resolving long-standing research-level conjectures.
breakthroughs.caveats: As with several 2026 AI-authored formal proofs, extracting streamlined human-readable expositions and testing the boundaries of related hyperlinear-group conjectures remain active follow-up work.

scoreRationale.foundational: Answers a 27-year central structural question in geometric group theory and symbolic dynamics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Clarifies the exact boundaries of sofic entropy, Gottschalk surjunctivity, and Kaplansky's direct finiteness conjecture.
scoreRationale.verification: Backed by a Lean formalization, though human distillation and broader textbook integration are ongoing.

breakthroughs.title: Claimed Refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH)
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: If confirmed, a subexponential algorithm for 3-SAT would overturn the foundational hardness assumption behind modern fine-grained complexity theory.
breakthroughs.summary: On October 26, 2026, OpenAI announced three major AI-assisted theoretical results—including a manuscript and public Lean formalization claiming a subexponential-time algorithm refuting the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), formulated by Impagliazzo and Paturi in 2001. ETH conjectures that 3-SAT requires 2^Ω(n) time and serves as the bedrock for hundreds of conditional lower bounds across graph algorithms, dynamic programming, and parameterized complexity.
technicalHighlights: Published alongside a public Lean formalization and algorithmic manuscript for community examination.
Even if valid, refuting ETH does not imply P = NP, as subexponential time (e.g., 2^o(n)) remains super-polynomial.
Triggered an intensive global audit by complexity theorists inspecting whether the Lean theorem statement matches classical 3-SAT complexity.
breakthroughs.caveats: Independent mathematical acceptance remains pending. Experts emphasize that even machine-checked proofs require human verification that the formal theorem matches the intended computational model without subtle specification loopholes.

scoreRationale.foundational: ETH is one of the most influential conjectures in theoretical computer science; refuting it would rewrite fine-grained complexity.
scoreRationale.ripple: Would topple or require revisiting hundreds of conditional lower bounds in parameterized and graph algorithms.
scoreRationale.verification: Marked down significantly because independent community audit of the Lean specification and algorithm is still active.
scoreRationale.velocity: An extraordinary surprise given that most complexity theorists strongly expected ETH to be true.

breakthroughs.title: Forced 3D Navier–Stokes Finite-Time Blowup Formal Proof
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Lean-verified construction of finite-time blowup for smoothly forced 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes—sparking intense debate over scope, priority, and Clay prize criteria.
breakthroughs.summary: On September 8, 2026, OpenAI released a writeup and Lean-verified formal proof demonstrating that a smooth solution to the 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations starting from rest under a specific smooth external forcing term can develop a singularity in finite time. While the formal Lean proof checked out, PDE specialists (including Tristan Buckmaster and Terence Tao's broader community) sparked a fierce priority and scope controversy—noting that the forced formulation bypasses the core unforced (zero-force) Millennium Prize mystery.
technicalHighlights: Constructed via massive multi-agent AI search and formalized in Lean 4.
Satisfies the literal wording of one branch of the official Clay Mathematics Institute forced-equation statement.
Became the defining case study of the 2026 'mathocalypse' debate over specification gaming vs. deep mathematical insight.
breakthroughs.caveats: Heavily contested on scientific scope and priority grounds: fluid-dynamics experts emphasize that constructing an artificial external force that drives blowup does not resolve the physically central unforced 3D Navier–Stokes regularity question.

scoreRationale.foundational: Mathematically non-trivial PDE construction, but scored below unforced Millennium resolutions due to the external-forcing caveat.
scoreRationale.ripple: Sparked sweeping reforms in how math communities define formal specifications and evaluate AI-authored proofs.
scoreRationale.verification: Lean-checked for the forced statement, yet actively disputed on priority, provenance, and Millennium-scope grounds.

breakthroughs.title: MatterGen: Property-Guided Generative Diffusion for Inorganic Crystals
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Shifts inorganic materials discovery from brute-force screening to inverse generative design—steering crystal structures directly toward target mechanical, magnetic, or electronic properties.
breakthroughs.summary: Published in Nature (Vol. 639) with open-source weights and code, Microsoft Research's MatterGen is a joint diffusion model over atomic species, coordinates, and unit-cell lattices across the periodic table. Fine-tuned adapter modules steer crystal generation toward specified band gaps, magnetic densities, or bulk moduli, doubling the rate of stable, unique, novel candidates compared to prior generative models.
technicalHighlights: Jointly diffuses discrete atom types, fractional coordinates, and continuous lattice geometry.
Supports multi-property conditioning (e.g., high magnetic density + low supply-chain-risk elements).
Open-source release (MIT) catalyzed a wave of inverse-design crystal diffusion models.
breakthroughs.caveats: An April 2026 Materials Horizons audit challenged the novelty of the flagship experimentally synthesized example (TaCr₂O₆, reported in 1972 literature and training sets), underscoring the gap between benchmark generation and genuinely unprecedented industrial materials.

breakthroughs.title: First One-Positron Quantum Cyclotron for Antimatter Precision Tests
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Traps a single antimatter positron for months and resolves its individual quantum states—enabling the sharpest-ever test of matter–antimatter (CPT) symmetry.
breakthroughs.summary: Physicists at Northwestern University demonstrated the first one-positron quantum cyclotron, isolating a single positron—the antimatter twin of the electron—for months inside a cryogenic Penning trap and resolving discrete quantum transitions between its cyclotron energy levels. Comparing the positron's magnetic moment against the electron's at part-per-trillion precision probes the deepest symmetry of the Standard Model (CPT invariance) and why the universe contains matter rather than equal antimatter.
technicalHighlights: Achieves months-long confinement and quantum-state control of an individual antimatter lepton.
Unlocks orders-of-magnitude sharper measurements of the positron anomalous magnetic moment.
Provides one of the cleanest low-energy probes of physics beyond the Standard Model.
breakthroughs.caveats: Full ultra-precision comparison of electron vs. positron magnetic moments requires ongoing multi-year systematic error reduction.
contributors: Northwestern Center for Fundamental Physics Team

breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Uses an optical cavity to restrict photon re-emission angles in organic solar cells, opening a practical thermodynamic path from the ~33% Shockley–Queisser ceiling toward ~43%.

By curbing radiative entropy losses, the photon-confinement mechanism lifts the single-junction efficiency ceiling beyond the classic 1961 Shockley–Queisser limit (~33%), charting a pathway toward ~43% single-junction efficiency without complex multi-junction stacking.

Demonstrated on organic photovoltaic architectures with broader relevance to thin-film and perovskite cells.
Theoretically lifts single-junction efficiency limits from ~33% toward ~43%.
breakthroughs.caveats: The 43% theoretical ceiling has not yet been achieved experimentally in a full commercial module; angular selectivity trades off against diffuse (cloudy-sky) sunlight capture.

breakthroughs.title: AlphaFold 2: Atomic-Accuracy Protein Structure Prediction (CASP14)
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Solved biology's 50-year protein structure prediction grand challenge at atomic accuracy—earning the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry and establishing the modern AI-for-science benchmark.
breakthroughs.summary: Validated at the blind CASP14 competition in November 2020 and published in Nature (July 2021), DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 introduced the Evoformer and equivariant structure modules to predict 3D atomic coordinates of proteins directly from amino-acid sequences with accuracy rivaling X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM. Releasing open source code and >200 million predicted structures in the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database permanently transformed structural biology and served as the blueprint for the entire 2020s wave of scientific AI.

Awarded half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (Demis Hassabis and John Jumper).
Open-source release and EMBL-EBI database unlocked >200 million structures used by millions of researchers worldwide.
breakthroughs.caveats: Predicts static single-chain conformations rather than dynamic conformational ensembles, multi-ligand complexes, or folding pathways—gaps subsequently targeted by AlphaFold 3 and generative biology models.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolved a 50-year grand challenge in molecular biology and proved deep learning can crack core scientific physics problems.
scoreRationale.ripple: One of the highest-impact scientific tools of the 21st century—directly catalyzing AlphaFold 3, AlphaProteo, Evo 2, and modern drug discovery.
scoreRationale.verification: Blind CASP14 benchmark victory, landmark Nature paper, tens of thousands of independent experimental confirmations, and the 2024 Nobel Prize.

breakthroughs.title: AlphaTensor: Reinforcement Learning Discovers Faster Matrix Multiplication

It improved the best-known scalar multiplication count for over 70 matrix sizes—including beating Volker Strassen's iconic 1969 49-multiplication 4×4 algorithm with 47 multiplications in finite-field arithmetic (ℤ₂)—while also optimizing hardware-specific GPU/TPU kernels.

Pioneered the autonomous algorithm-discovery lineage culminating in FunSearch (2023) and AlphaEvolve (2025).

breakthroughs.title: First Laboratory Nuclear Fusion Ignition (Target Gain Q = 1.5)
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: First controlled laboratory fusion experiment to produce more fusion energy (3.15 MJ) than the laser energy delivered to the fuel target (2.05 MJ)—proving ignition physics works.
breakthroughs.summary: On December 5, 2022 (published in Physical Review Letters in February 2024), scientists at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory's National Ignition Facility achieved inertial confinement fusion ignition with a target gain of G = 1.5, generating 3.15 megajoules of fusion yield from 2.05 megajoules of ultraviolet laser energy. Culminating six decades of fusion physics research, NIF subsequently replicated and surpassed the milestone multiple times.
technicalHighlights: First controlled experiment in history to exceed scientific breakeven (target gain > 1) and the Lawson ignition criterion.
Replicated multiple times at even higher yields in 2023–2025, confirming robust burning-plasma physics.
Provides an indispensable experimental anchor for calibrating 2024–2026 clean-energy and physics breakthroughs.
breakthroughs.caveats: Target gain compares fusion yield to laser energy hitting the hohlraum, not the ~300 MJ wall-plug electrical energy consumed by the 1970s-design flashlamp lasers; commercial fusion power requires orders-of-magnitude higher engineering gain and repetition rate.

scoreRationale.foundational: Decisively proved controlled laboratory nuclear fusion ignition is physically achievable after six decades of effort.
scoreRationale.ripple: Catalyzed billions in public/private inertial and magnetic fusion engineering and burning-plasma research.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Physical Review Letters (132, 065102) and experimentally repeated multiple times at NIF.

breakthroughs.title: Discovery of the Aperiodic Monotile ('The Hat' / Einstein Tile)
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Solved the 60-year 'einstein' problem in geometry by discovering a single 13-sided polygon ('the hat') that tiles the infinite plane exclusively in non-repeating patterns.
breakthroughs.summary: Hobbyist mathematician David Smith together with Joseph Samuel Myers, Craig S. Kaplan, and Chaim Goodman-Strauss solved the decades-old aperiodic monotile problem by exhibiting 'the hat'—a simple 13-sided polykite—and a continuum of related shapes that tile the Euclidean plane without ever admitting a periodic tiling. Shortly afterward, the same team discovered 'the spectre', a strictly chiral aperiodic monotile requiring no mirror reflections.
technicalHighlights: Settles a 60-year open geometry problem descending from Hao Wang (1961) and Roger Penrose's two-tile aperiodic tilings (1974).
Combines a clean human geometric incommensurability proof with a computer-assisted combinatorial verification.
Remains a celebrated calibration anchor for pure human mathematical creativity alongside 2024–2026 AI proofs.
breakthroughs.caveats: The original 'hat' tile used reflected copies; the authors quickly resolved that caveat in May 2023 with the reflection-free chiral 'spectre' monotile.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolved one of the most iconic, accessible open problems in discrete geometry since the 1960s.
scoreRationale.ripple: Sparked immediate work across quasicrystals, metamaterials, spectral geometry, and recreational mathematics.
scoreRationale.verification: Dual independent proofs (geometric + computer-assisted), peer-reviewed in Combinatorial Theory, and universally accepted.

Beat 20-year best-known constructions on the cap set problem and improved classical online bin-packing baselines.
Discovered short, human-interpretable Python programs rather than opaque black-box solutions.
